title: Field install standup — spotlight notes (Nov 30 2026)
summary: Concise capture of the Nov 30 field install standup focused on two active customer installs (AcmeHealth and BlueLedger), a networking regression observed after the runtime update, and a persistent KMS handshake flake. Contains quick troubleshooting notes, immediate mitigations, and owners for follow-ups.
meeting_notes: Quick status: AcmeHealth site (onprem) — core services up, inference runtime passing smoke tests, but intermittent request 504s during high-concurrency tests.
BlueLedger VPC — deployment mostly completed; observed broken egress to telemetry endpoint due to new outbound ACL rule applied by customer's infra team yesterday.
Observed regression after runtime 2.7.1 -> 2.7.2: increased connection churn on control-plane sidecar when sequence lengths > 4k. Repro locally with stress harness.
KMS handshake: several installs report TLS alert 40 during initial KMS prot exchange. Suspect library upgrade in vault-client (v1.18.0) — rolling back helps but not fully consistent.
Field engineer notes (Sofia): on AcmeHealth rack 3, NIC offload settings mismatched (RX/TX offload disabled by server vendor image) causing noticeable CPU spikes under batch sizes > 32.
Customer ask: AcmeHealth requests temporary rate-limiter quota increase during their onboarding perf runs — need approval from capacity planning and cost estimate for burst window.
Security sign-off: BlueLedger wants confirmation that private CA cert chain will be preserved during next patch window; engineering to provide a short checklist for their infra team.
SRE FYI: NTP skew on AcmeHealth edge node showed 12s drift; caused token validation errors intermittently. NTP fix applied and retested.
Decided to open a focused incident for the runtime control-plane regression; owners assigned below. Not elevating to P0 yet since functionality still available with higher latency.

Live debugging plan: capture tcpdump + kvcache metrics at 10s interval for next 3 runs; correlate with sidecar logs and kernel drop counters. Dmitri to coordinate remote capture with on-site engineer.
blockers: KMS TLS alert 40 during handshake prevents automated key provisioning for new installs — blocks onboarding for two customers until we confirm a safe workaround.

Outbound ACL change at BlueLedger prevents telemetry uploads; customer infra team blocked our attempt to add temporary egress because of policy review — need policy exception or alternate telemetry endpoint.
Runtime 2.7.2 regression increases connection churn under long context loads; blocks performance signoff on AcmeHealth until mitigated or reverted.
Vendor server image at AcmeHealth disables NIC offloads by default; lack of vendor cooperation for a rebuild delays sustainable performance testing (vendor ticket open).

Sofia: coordinate with AcmeHealth infra to request temporary rate-limit increase and provide cost estimate for 36h burst — due 2026-12-01 EOD.
Maya: prepare short CA cert preservation checklist for BlueLedger (includes steps to export, validate chain, and patch plan) — share with security and BlueLedger by 2026-12-02.
Liam: validate rollback patch for vault-client (v1.17.x) across internal testbed and write playbook for customers if rollback is required — due 2026-12-02.
Inez: schedule weekday window with vendor to enable NIC offloads on AcmeHealth's images; collect exact BIOS/driver versions for compatibility matrix — due 2026-12-03.
Eng-sre: add a short-term telemetry fallback to buffering + s3-upload for BlueLedger if egress exception is not granted within 24h — implement feature flag by 2026-12-02.
All: capture tcpdump + kvcache metrics for next 3 load tests and upload to /shared/field-captures/nov30/ — owner Dmitri, due 2026-12-01 morning.
decisions: Do not roll back runtime globally yet; open incident and gate rollback to customers impacted while fix is developed.
Approve temporary quota bump for AcmeHealth for a narrowly scoped 36-hour window pending cost confirmation.
Use a telemetry buffering fallback for BlueLedger if policy exception not approved within 24 hours.
Prepare a targeted vendor compatibility note rather than broad vendor escalation to avoid blocking installs elsewhere.
observations: Most onprem installs surface edge-specific infra quirks (NIC settings, NTP, BIOS versions) more than platform code bugs — suggests we need a compact preflight checklist for field engineers.
KMS flake correlates with a small percentage of installs using older TLS stacks; rollback helps in many but not all cases — may be multi-factor.
Control-plane sidecar churn appears only when host-level cryptographic accel (AES-NI) is absent; hypothesis: software crypto path increases CPU, impacts keepalive handling.
Customers prefer a clear temporary mitigation path (e.g., quota bump, buffering) rather than waiting for a full patch — operational playbooks should list these options clearly.
next_steps: Run controlled perf job replicating AcmeHealth traffic pattern with sequence lengths 3k, 6k, 9k to reproduce control-plane churn and gather flamegraphs — Dmitri assigned.
Prepare a customer-friendly bulletin summarizing risk, mitigation, and expected ETA for permanent fix — Maya to draft and review with comms.
Add 'preflight-check: nic-offload, ntp, tls-lib' to installer preflight output and fail with actionable remediation notes rather than a generic error — backlog ticket JIRA-7142.
Confirm telemetry fallback implementation and test end-to-end with BlueLedger staging environment before rolling to prod flag.
